chunks: [A part of the same sermon :] (Before this Enjoiner of Good, matters will deteriorate) till war will rage among you with full force,
showing forth its teeth, with udders full of sweet milk but with a sour tip.
Beware, it will be tomorrow and the morrow will come soon with things which you do not know.
The Man in power, not from this crowd, will take to task all those were formerly appointed for their ill deeds
and the earth will pour forth its internal treasures and fling before him easily her keys.
He will show you the just way of behaviour and revive the Qur’ān and sunnah which have become lifeless (among people).

key_terms.الْوَالِي: The ruler / The Man in power

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the era preceding the rise of the Just Enforcer in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha’s 'Foretelling Events' chapter vividly depicts the pre-Mahdi era of political decay, where rulers exploit the earth's treasures and officials act unjustly. It highlights the imminent arrival of the Just Enforcer (al-Mahdi), who will restore true justice and revive the dormant practices of the Quran and Sunnah, a core eschatological belief in Shia tradition. The imagery of 'war on a leg' and 'sweet milk' symbolizes the deceptive ease of power acquisition before the final establishment of divine rule.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [A part of the same sermon :] (Before this Enjoiner of Good, [1] matters will deteriorate) till war will rage among you with full force,
showing forth its teeth, with udders full of sweet milk but with a sour tip.
Beware, it will be tomorrow and the morrow will come soon with things which you do not know.
The Man in power, not from this crowd, will take to task all those were formerly appointed for their ill deeds
and the earth will pour forth its iternal treasures and fling before him easily her keys.
He will show you the just way of behaviour and revive the Qur’ān and sunnah which have become lifeless (among people).
